items.title: Mike Davis interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, April 1, 2024
items.q: I was listening to a Michael Brecker record a few days ago

ctx.x: He said, “An essential part of real musicianship as an improviser or composer is the ability to use any note on the chromatic scale on any chord and make it sound believable.”

I think that’s a great quote, I mean and Bill can do that himself. I mean he’s an incredible musician and educator as well. Yeah I totally agree with that, and certain people are so fluid at it. I was listening to a Michael Brecker record a few days ago and I’m like what is he playing on that. And it’s like he’s playing a major third on a minor chord and it sounds like a million bucks. And I don’t know exactly why that’s working like that — but I mean I kind of know why it is but certain players just have that…
Yeah. Miles Davis — you know something about with his Harmon mute it’s almost like he could play anything and somehow it’s like, “Yeah that’s great.”
